check: She drives 30 × 10 = 300 miles and earns 300 × $0.50 = $150. Gas costs (300 ÷ 10) × $2 = $60, leaving $150 − $60 = $90.
error_description: The gas-cost calculation multiplies miles by dollars per gallon without converting miles to gallons using 10 miles per gallon. This produces an incorrect fuel expense and net earnings.
